newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall St boosts Euro shares, dollar holds firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall St boosts Euro shares, dollar holds firm.

text.p: European shares strode higher in early trade on Friday after Wall Street rang up its 30th closing high of the year and political tension in Russia continued to support the dollar.
London's FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 10.4 points at 4,052.5 by 0930 GMT, not far from its best ever level of 4,063.2 which was set on Tuesday.
"We're likely to continue onwards and upwards," said one dealer, "But not with too much gusto."

Traders said the main force driving the market was Wall Street's 38.39 point rise to 6,059.20 after signs of an economic softening from the latest batch of U.S. data lessened the odds that U.S. interest rates will be raised soon.
British gilts had also opened stronger lending support to equities.

But superstitious investors were wary of the approach of Saturday's anniversary of the 1987 stock market crash. The month of October features heavily in stock market jitters, also being the month of the 1929 Wall Street crash.
The bias in the market remained bullish however, said Tom Pelc, technical analyst at MMS International.

"The market is still positive, but the trend is not that firm," Pelc said. "We can still go higher, but the move will be Frence's blue-chip CAC-40 share index opened higher and climbed some 0.7 percent, before slipping back after making a high for the year of 2,182.38 points. The market was propelled by Wall Street's rise and rising bond prices,traders said.

"People are feeling very optimistic and the market's testing 2,185 (points), which is a very important point in the charts. If we rise above it convincingly, the market would be poised to breach 2,200," a trader said. Wall Street also pushed German shares to a new high of 2,737.51 in bourse trading, before they, too, fell back.
Continuing fallout from the power struggle in Moscow after President Boris Yeltsin sacked security chief Alexander Lebed on Thursday did not deter buyers.

Germany's geographical proximity and economic links to Russia sometimes is less unsettling for German shares than for the mark as investors sell marks for dollars, seen as a safe haven in times of trouble.
In early European trade, the dollar backed off a fresh 4-1/2 month high at 1.5454 marks set Thursday after the Lebed sacking, but was well supported above 1.54 marks.
While the situation in Russia now appeared calm, traders said they would be wary, particularly on a Friday, and as a result reluctant to be long in marks.
Traders were also digesting further signs of a steady recovery in west German economic activity.
The Ifo research institute said its September business climate index for west Germany rose to 95.7 from 94.4 in August and slightly higher than prior forecasts at about 95.0.

"You've got to ask yourself whether the Ifo index will force the Bundesbank closer to tightening (interest rates) and I think the answer will be no," said Adrian Schmidt, economist at Chase Investment Bank.

The dollar was robust against the yen in early trading and set a fresh 33-month high at 112.63 amid a renewed bout of yen weakness ahead of the U.S. trade data and the Japanese general election on Sunday.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5422 marks and 112.47 yen compared with 1.5436 marks and 112.25 yen in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
London - The FTSE index was up 10.4 points, or 0.26 percent, at 4,052.5.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index was up 15.08 points at 2,731.34, or 0.56 percent.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was up 14.59 points, or 0.67 percent, at 2,179.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $379.60 after closing on Thursday in Europe at $380.45.
